The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- from the respondents for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident that took place on 23.05.2022.
2.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioner as follows:
On 23.05.2022, at about 10.00 a.m. when he was riding the motor cycle bearing No.KA-03-KH-0334, on Hosakote- Sidlaghatta Road, Thereyuru Dinne, Sulibele Hobli, Bengaluru Rural district, at that time driver of the lorry bearing Reg.
No.TN-29-BF-5096 by driving the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner's motor cycle, caused the accident, due to which he sustained injuries.

It is stated that he has spent huge amount for his treatment,
medicine etc.,
3.

It is further stated that prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and was studying MBA at Nagarjuna College, Mudugurki, Chikkaballapura and also doing agriculture and salesman and earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is not able to attend his classes and also unable to do his work as doing earlier.
It is stated that the accident in question was due to the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry bearing Reg. No. TN-29-BF-5096.
Hence, the 1st respondent being the owner and 2nd respondent being the insurer of the offending lorry are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

sentences.text: On service of notice, the respondent No.2 has entered appearance through its learned counsel and filed written statement.

Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 remained absent and hence,
he was placed exparte.
5. The 2nd respondent in its objection statement has denied all the petition averments and contended that the petition itself is not maintainable either on facts or law.

It has denied the age,
income and occupation of the petitioner and also the amount spent towards the medical expenses by the petitioner.
It has denied the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Lorry bearing Reg.
No.TN-29-BF-5096 and also the valid and effective driving licence held by the drive of the offending vehicle
. The offending lorry was not having valid permit, FC and RC as on the date of the accident.
Owner of the vehicle and the jurisdictional police have not complied section 134(C)and 158(6) of M.V. Act.
It is further contended that the accident was occurred due to the negligence of the rider of the motor cycle.
The compensation and interest claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
Hence on all other grounds, it has sought for dismissal of the petition.

6. Based on the pleadings, my predecessor in office has framed following issues :-
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 23.05.2022, at about 10.00 a.m. when he was proceeding by riding his Activa bearing Reg. No.KA-03-KH-0334 and reached near Thereyuru Dinne, Hosakote-Sidlagatta Road, Sulibele Hobli, Bengaluru Rural district, at that time driver of the lorry bearing Reg. No.TN-29- BF-5096 by driving the same at very high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the vehicle in which the petitioner was proceeding, as a result petitioner sustained injuries?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, from whom and how much?
3. What order or award?
7. In order to prove the case, the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and examined one witness as PW.2 and got marked 24 documents as per Ex.P1 to 24.
On the other hand, respondent No.2 has not led its defence evidence.

8. Heard the arguments and perused the written argument submitted by the respondent No.2 and perused the documents.
9.

My findings on the above issues as under:-
 Issue No.1 ... In the Affirmative

,
 Issue No.2 ...

Partly in the affirmative,

sentences.text: 3  REASONS 10. Issues No.1 to 3:

As per the case of the petitioner, On 23.05.2022, at about 10.00 a.m. when he was proceeding as rider on motor cycle bearing No. KA-03-KH-0334, on Hosakote-Sidlagatta Road,
Thereyuru Dinne, Sulibele Hobli, Bengaluru Rural district, at that time driver of the lorry bearing Reg. No.TN-29-BF-5096 by driving the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner's motor cycle, caused the accident, due to which he sustained injuries.

The petitioner in order to prove his case, got examined himself as PW.1 and reiterated the averments of the petition and got marked F.I.R, F.I.S, Spot Mahazar, IMV report, Wound certificate and Charge sheet as per Ex.P1 to 6.
11.
I have carefully examined the entire oral and documentary evidence available on record.
The incident said to have taken place on 23.05.2022 at 10.00 a.m.
On 25.05.2022 first information was lodged by the father of the petitioner.

Ex.P3 is the spot mahazar, this document makes it clear that accident occurred in the left side of the road, and also the said road width is 22 feet, accident occurred from 5 feet of left side road edge.
On perusal of charge sheet and other document discloses that the driver of the lorry hit against the petitioner's vehicle from front side while petitioner was proceeding on his way.
Driver of the lorry has not taken proper care and precaution regarding the vehicles which are plying on the main road and taken his vehicle extreme right and hit against the petitioner's motorcycle.
If he had taken proper care and caution and driven the lorry in a slow manner, he could avoid the accident.
The Respondent No.1 has not led evidence to establish that there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry and to establish that the accident occurred sole negligence of the petitioner.
12. The respondents have not raised any contention with regard to the negligence aspect.
Still the petitioner has deposed about the manner of accident.
There are no reason to distrust the evidence of petitioner.
Therefore, I hold that the accident was occurred only due to the rash and negligent act of driver of the offending lorry bearing Reg. No. TN-29-BF-5096.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:
While answering issue No.1, I have already observed that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of lorry bearing Reg. No. TN-29- BF-5096.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for the compensation.

14. LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS ON ACCOUNT OF PERMANENT DISABILITY:
It is the case of the petitioner that prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and was MBA student and also doing agriculture and salesman and earning Rs.15,000/-
p.m.

In order to prove the same, petitioner has produced Ex.P8 to P13 which are marks cards and course completion certificate issued by Nagarjuna College which shows that the petitioner has completed MBA in the year 2022-23.
It is also the contention of the petitioner that he was doing agriculture and salesman work, but he has not produced any document to show his income.

Hence, this tribunal has Anil Kumar .K vs Manickavasagam .P on 6 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167435200/
4 considered the notional income of the petitioner.

sentences.text: The incident occurred during the year 2022.
Considering the avocation and the year of the accident, I deem it just and proper to consider the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.15,500/- per month.
The petitioner claims that he is unable to work due to the injuries sustained to him.
The petitioner got examined the Doctor as PW.2.

In the evidence of doctor, he has deposed that petitioner sustained head injury having occipital bone fracture maxilla/orbital bone fracture with diffuse axonal injury, fracture both bones of left leg upper third.
He underwent CRIF with IMIL nailing of Tibia.,
On presentation the petitioner is complaints of pain and difficulty in walking and climbing stairs, inability to squat and sit cross legged.
On examination petitioner walks with pain and limping wasting of left thigh and diffuse swelling of left leg is seen and the fractures of both bones of left leg are united.

He assessed 37% disability to the left lower limb and 18%
whole body disability of the petitioner.
While calculating the loss of future income on account of permanent disability, the functional disability to the whole body has to be considered.
The disability to the whole body shall have to be assessed on the basis of the profession of the injured and relative effect of the disability to his profession.
The injuries sustained by the petitioner are not in dispute and the injuries sustained by him definitely will have an impact on his work.
PW.2 doctor has also stated that the fractures are united.

Hence,
considering the nature of the work and impact of disability on his performance, I deem it just and proper to consider 10% disability to his whole body.
It is contended that petitioner was aged 22 years as on the date of accident.
The accident occurred on 23.05.2022.
However, by considering the age mentioned in the date of birth mentioned in Ex.P7 Adhaar card as 17.11.1999, the petitioner was aged 22 years at the time of accident.
The multiplier applicable to the age of 22 is 18 as per the case of Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation(AIR 2009 SC 3104).

15. PAIN AND SUFFERINGS:
As per wound certificate produced at Ex.P5, the petitioner has sustained injuries of Occipital bone fracure of maxilar/orbital wall fractures, fracture both bone upper 1/3rd, multiple abrasions all over the body and nose and ear bleed and the doctor has opined that the above injuries are grievous in nature.
The Ex.P14 Discharge Summary of Prolife hospital reveals that petitioner was treated as an inpatient in the said hospital from 23.05.2022 to 06.06.2022 and underwent treatment.

Considering these aspects, I deem it just and proper to award Rs.50,000/- towards pain and Anil Kumar .K vs Manickavasagam .P on 6 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167435200/
5 sufferings.

sentences.text: 16. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has produced medical bills worth Rs.79,295/- as per Ex.P15, advance payment receipts at Ex.P16 to 18 and medical prescriptions at Ex.P19.
I have examined the medical bills and receipts.

Since the petitioner was treated as inpatient and undergone treatment, there are no reasons to disbelieve the amount spent by the petitioner to the tune of Rs.79,295/- and he is entitled for the same.

17. ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD & NOURISHMENT AND OTHER INCIDENTAL EXPENSES:
As the petitioner was treated as an inpatient for a period of 14 days, certainly he might have spent amount towards conveyance, attendant charges, nourishing food and other incidental expenses and also at the time of subsequent follow up treatment.
Considering these aspects, I deem it proper to award Rs.14,000/- under this head.

18. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment given and duration of his stay in the hospital
, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least 3 months.

Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner,
this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.46,500/-
(15,500X3) under this head.

19. LOSS OF AMENITIES IN LIFE/LIFE COMFORTS AND EXPECTANCY OF LIFE/MARRIAGE PROSPECTUS:
The petitioner was aged about 22 years at the time accident and on account of accident, he has to suffer the above disability.
He has to suffer this discomfort and sacrifice the amenities through out his remaining life.
This court has considered disability to the extent of 10% to whole body.
Considering all these aspects, I deem it proper to award Rs.50,000/- on this head.

20. FUTURE MEDICAL AND OTHER INCIDENTAL EXPENSES : The doctor has not suggested anything about the future surgery to be undergone by the petitioner, hence petitioner is not entitled for compensation under this head.
21.

Thus in all, the petitioner entitled for the compensation as here under:

In total, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,74,595/-.

Interest:
The petitioner is claiming interest @ 9% p.a. on the compensation amount.

Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding future medical expenses) is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
23. Liability:

Regarding fixation of liability is concerned, I have already observed that the accident was taken place due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry bearing Reg. No.
TN-29-BF-5096.
The breach of any of the policy conditions are not proved.
It is not disputed that 1st respondent is the owner and 2nd respondent is the insurer.
Hence, 1st respondent being the owner and 2 nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The 2 nd respondent being the insurer shall indemnify the 1st respondent in payment of compensation amount.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
24. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2, I pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,74,595/-(Rupees Five lakhs seventy four thousand five hundred and ninety five only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realisation.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit of the compensation amount, 60% of the award amount shall be paid to him through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification and due verification and further 40% of the award amount shall be kept in FD in favour of Anil Kumar .K vs Manickavasagam .P
